question: The function g is a rational function defined by g(x) = f(x)/(x + 2), where f is a quadratic function. The y-intercept of the graph of f is (0,10), and g passes through the points shown in the table: (1,5) and (4,7). What is g(3)?
structure: Several facts about one function with unknown coefficients: f is quadratic with f(0)=10 and g(x)=f(x)/(x+2) with two known g-values; fits the "Unknown parameter regression" / "Packed-conditions regression" pattern.

candidates.name: Packed-conditions regression on g(x) built from f(x) with f(0) known
candidates.humanWork: Understand that f(x)=ax^2+bx+10 (since f(0)=10) and translate g(1)=5, g(4)=7 into regression conditions; then read fitted a,b and evaluate g(3).
candidates.desmosWork: Fit parameters a and b from the two paired conditions y_{1}~(a x_{1}^2 + b x_{1} + 10)/(x_{1}+2), then compute g(3) directly from the fitted a and b.
candidates.validityNote: Two independent conditions (g at x=1 and x=4) determine the two unknowns a and b uniquely; regression on x_{1}=[1,4] is deterministic and reliable.

candidates.name: Slider-search on integer coefficients for f(x)
candidates.humanWork: Set integer sliders for a and b (if integers are plausible), plot g and adjust until g(1)=5 and g(4)=7, then read g(3).
candidates.desmosWork: Visual search via sliders; automates evaluation but requires dragging and may be slower or non-reusable when a,b noninteger.
candidates.validityNote: Works only if a and b happen to be integers in a small range; less reliable and more effort than regression.

candidates.name: Two-equation bracket regression (copy each g-equation into bracket form)
candidates.humanWork: Translate g(1)=5 and g(4)=7 into two bracketed expressions and regress them simultaneously for a and b, then evaluate g(3).
candidates.desmosWork: Solves a and b from aligned bracket regression and computes g(3).
candidates.validityNote: Equivalent in effect to candidate C1 but uses bracket list form; also deterministic and reliable.

solution.why: f(0)=10 lets write f(x)=ax^2+bx+10; use regression on the two given g-values to find a and b, then evaluate g(3) = f(3)/(3+2).

expressions.purpose: paired list of the x-values where g is known
paired list of the corresponding g(x) outputs
regress to determine the unknown quadratic coefficients a and b in f(x)=ax^2+bx+10 so that g(x)=f(x)/(x+2) fits the two given points
evaluate g(3)=f(3)/(3+2) using the fitted a and b

result.detail: g(3)=31/5 = 6.2 computed from fitted a and b
